OVERSOUL: The all-containing soul. [R.] That unity, that oversout, within which every man's particular being is contained and made one with all other. Emerson.

OVERRAKE: To rake over, or sweep across, from end to end, as waves that break over a vessel anchored with head to the sea.
OPEN-MOUTHED: Having the mouth open; gaping; hence, greedy; clamorous. L'Estrange.
OBSTETRICIOUS: Serving to assist childbirth; obstetric; hence, facilitating any bringing forth or deliverance. [Obs.] Yet is all human teaching but maieutical, or obstetricious. Cudworth.

OUTERMOST: Being on the extreme external part; farthest outward; as, the outermost row. Boyle.
OPHIOMORPHOUS: Having the form of a serpent.

OVERPRESS: 1. To bear upon with irresistible force; to crush; to overwhelm. Shak. 2. To overcome by importunity. Johnson.
OVERPRESSURE: Excessive pressure or urging. London Athenæum.
ORARIAN: Of or pertaining to a coast.

OUGHTNESS: The state of being as a thing ought to be; rightness. [R.] N. W. Taylor.

OPISTHOPULMONATE: Having the pulmonary sac situated posteriorly; -- said of certain air-breathing Mollusca.
OBLIGATORILY: In an obligatory manner; by reason of obligation. Foxe.
OLEA: A genus of trees including the olive. Note: The Chinese Olea fragrans, noted for its fragrance, and the American devilwood (Olea Americana) are now usually referred to another genus (Osmanthus).

OUAKARI: Any South American monkey of the genus Brachyurus, especially B. ouakari.

OPAQUENESS: The state or quality of being impervious to light; opacity. Dr. H. More.

OSLO: The capital and most populous city of Norway.
